subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): sandboxed sub-agents could read other agents' bridged memory through shared vault wiki reads

question: Should sandboxed callers in a global Memory Wiki vault be permanently restricted to their own bridge-owned pages and unowned/shared pages, while non-sandboxed callers retain cross-agent global-vault reads?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes an existing sandboxed read behavior to enforce a security boundary without adding a compatibility toggle; source and proof support the implementation, but the permanent supported sharing contract requires owner intent.

options.title: Confirm sandbox isolation and merge
options.body: Confirm that sandboxed cross-agent bridge reads are unsupported in global vault mode, then merge after required checks and a current-base refresh.

options.title: Require an explicit compatibility mode
options.body: Pause this patch and define a documented, opt-in legacy sharing policy if sandboxed cross-agent bridge access must remain supported for existing deployments.

recommendation.title: Confirm sandbox isolation and merge
recommendation.body: Confirm that sandboxed cross-agent bridge reads are unsupported in global vault mode, then merge after required checks and a current-base refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the merged vault-scoping and bridge-ownership model that defines the surrounding compatibility boundary.
